text.p: TORONTO, Aug 7 Reuter) - The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE GLOBE AND MAIL: Ontario unveils services shift: Tory plans, seen as step toward GTA supergovernment, set battle lines with municipalities
-TTC fire sends 33 to hospital: Rail-yard smoke from burning rubber pours into Bloor-Danforth tunnel
-Lithuania looks to West: Alliance seen as nation's key to independence
-Apple shocks supporters with Microsoft alliance: Deal ends bitter rivalry between two computer companies
-Missing wife found dead: Husband charged with murder
-Premiers' united front crumbling: Little harmony on pace of decentralization, handling of Quebec question
Report on Business Section: NorTel wins German deal: Beats top European rivals on a network contract that the company hopes will showcase its expertise
-Air Canada boosts U.S. presence: Service to 3 more cities seen as pre-emptive strike against American Airlines' new access to Canada
-Teleglobe unit wins bid to launch wireless cable TV: Financial resources, expertise cited
-Losses continue to bedevil Roayal Oak mines: Shutdown of mine in NWT leads to another writedown
-AlphaStar signs off in latest satellite setback
THE FINANCIAL POST: Apple links with Microsoft: Long-time rival injects US$150 million into struggling Apple. Steve Jobs powers back and joins other industry big-hitters in shakeup of board.
-Software loophole is deleted: Industry may be hit hard by loss of financing from $1B tax shelter
